findings.title: Non-atomic match_count increment and DB write inside validator
findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count and saves the record on every call. This method is invoked from EmailValidator during User validation, which can run multiple times per signup (e.g., user.valid? before save, then again during save). Each validation attempt will increment match_count multiple times, leading to inaccurate statistics. Concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email will also suffer from lost updates because the increment is not atomic (no lock or update_all). This causes race conditions and corrupts match_count data. The method should either be split into a pure predicate and a separate tracking method, or use atomic increments (e.g., increment!(:match_count, touch: :last_match_at) with a transaction).

findings.title: Validation triggers unnecessary database writes for do_nothing action
findings.body: EmailValidator calls BlockedEmail.should_block? during validation. Even when the blocked email's action_type is :do_nothing (meaning the email should not be blocked), should_block? still executes a database update (incrementing match_count and saving). This causes writes on every signup attempt for emails that are merely being tracked, which can degrade performance under load and violates the principle that validators should be side-effect-free. The validator should only query for the record's action_type without updating it, or the tracking update should be moved to a separate explicit call after validation.

findings.title: No tests for domain whitelist/blacklist logic in EmailValidator
findings.body: The new EmailValidator replaces the previous email_validator method in User, which handled email domain whitelist and blacklist restrictions. The spec file only tests blocked email behavior, leaving the whitelist/blacklist logic untested. If a regression were introduced in that logic, no test would catch it. Tests should be added to verify that whitelist and blacklist settings correctly add or don't add errors to the email attribute.
